workload_boundary_policy.support_authority: workloads are measurement and provenance rows; canonical support must be cited through owner_splits
workload_boundary_policy.generated_artifact_rule: docs, command-surface, reports, and cache package workloads are generated or provenance-only unless a phase owner claims behavior
workload_boundary_policy.retired_surface_rule: fallback, shim, old-mode, compatibility, unsupported, and alternate acceptance rows map to canonical_rejection

workloads.support_boundary: whole-compiler timing only; phase support is owned by parser, sema, lowering, IR, and e2e split indexes
workloads.objective: measure one live wrapper-driven compile without cache reuse

workloads.support_boundary: cache-hit timing and artifact provenance only; cache reuse is not a compatibility support claim
workloads.objective: measure truthful wrapper cache restoration with compile-output provenance preserved

workloads.support_boundary: macro-host and import cache invalidation provenance only; stale-cache, fallback, or recovery-positive behavior maps to canonical rejection
workloads.objective: measure cache reuse and invalidation over a source that already publishes macro-host and import surfaces

workloads.support_boundary: runtime-acceptance subsurface only; macro-host cache publication cannot establish fallback or alternate runtime support
workloads.objective: keep macro-host cache publication tied to the live runtime-acceptance path

workloads.support_boundary: generated documentation provenance only; docs generation cannot define behavior support
workloads.objective: measure the checked-in native docs generator instead of synthetic markdown transforms

workloads.support_boundary: generated command-surface provenance only; command rendering cannot create compatibility support
workloads.objective: measure the generated operator-facing command appendix

workloads.support_boundary: runner ownership and duplicate-loop evidence only; overlap rows that mention recovery or fallback stay rejection/provenance
workloads.objective: keep heavyweight suite ownership explicit so duplicate recovery-negative loops can be removed
